newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-INJURY COULD KEEP GASCOIGNE OUT ALL SEASON.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-INJURY COULD KEEP GASCOIGNE OUT ALL SEASON.

text.p: England face playing their next two World Cup qualifiers without midfielder Paul Gascoigne after doctors decided to put his injured ankle in plaster again, British newspapers said on Saturday.

Gascoigne could miss the rest of the season because his left ankle, injured during a six-a-side tournament in the Netherlands in January, had not healed, they said. His Scottish club Rangers said Gascoigne saw a specialist on Thursday and would have to keep the new plaster on for at least 10 days.
After that, he would have to rest the ankle for another three weeks, the Daily Mail newspaper said.

Rangers assistant manager Archie Knox told the Daily Mirror: "The ankle joint was really shaken up and the bruising to the bone went very deep. There is no ligament damage but we shall be keeping a careful eye on him."
England have World Cup qualifiers at home against Georgia on April 30 and away to Poland on May 31.
